[h1][b]休闲风的小飞船类幸存者[/b][/h1] [h1]前言[/h1] 非常不错的一款类幸存者游戏，《Cozy Space Survivors》中玩家可以驾驶奇奇怪怪的飞船翱翔于太空，对抗源源不断的敌人，收集爱心与巧克力，帮助这里的居民并收获真挚的感谢。 [h1]拟真的飞船设计[/h1] 开始游戏后系统会提示选择飞船，目前一共有4艘，游戏也是为其起了可爱的名字，分别为咻咻、呲呲、瞅瞅与虫虫。 目前我解锁了前两艘，咻咻各方面能力比较均衡，适合用来上手练习，呲呲体型巨大生命力更好但移动速度缓慢，其可以装备更多的武器。 本作的飞船控制较为拟真，飞船拥有惯性，也就是起步和停止时都有个缓冲阶段，然后转向时飞船船头会旋转到对应方位然后才开始加速移动。 这种操纵方式也不算罕见了，稍微熟悉下就能上手，前期移动速度还未提升上来时多留意下碰撞体积即可。 [h1]趣味的任务系统[/h1] 游戏的场景设置在浩瀚的太空之中，和《吸血鬼幸存者》类似，生存特定时间即可，这期间敌人会不断袭来，而玩家也可以自由探索。 本作最与众不同的点也正于此，场景中除了散落着回复品和经验值（爱心）等道具外，还有着诸多NPC，这些NPC大多需要玩家提供帮助。 任务类型也是多种多样，从寻找特定道具、寻找走失的NPC带回去到清理附近敌人、清理散落在太空中的地雷等等。 这些任务可以同时接取多个，完成后会获得大量经验奖励。 其中有一个有意思的任务是帮助GO和DOT相遇，连在一起就是GODOT，一个新兴的开源游戏引擎，火爆一时的《土豆兄弟》就是用这个引擎开发的，这里算是个小彩蛋。 实际游玩过程中，会发现游戏没有地图设计，这就导致飞来飞去完成了某些任务但是找不到起初接取任务的地方了。 游戏的构筑也比较爽快，度过前期1-2分钟的艰难时期外，便可以享受刷刷刷的割草体验了。 [h1]结语[/h1] 整体而言，本作带来的游戏体验非常不错，喜欢此类游戏又玩腻了几个知名的类幸存者的话，《Cozy Space Survivors》是个不错的选择。 [code]双语评测，认准我们： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]双语评测[/url] Make Chinese and English speaker feel at home： [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35263058-Bilingual-Curator/]Bilingual Curator[/url][/code]

[h1] 🚀👾 Cozy Space Survivors 🚀👾 [/h1] .. offers a nice balance between relaxing and rogue-lite gameplay. You manage your resources and survive in the most charming auto-hitter game. The progression feels rewarding without ever becoming overwhelming. Each session brings new challenges with different ,,ships’’ and discoveries, making it a fresh joy to play. You have to do little quests for the Space-Habitants and collect chocolate to buy the upgrades for your ship and health. Its exactly whats being promised, a ,,cozy rouge-lite you can play through and get all the archievements. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3260935530 [b] Graphics: [/b] The visual style is cute and cozy. The colors are vibrant, and the designs are lovingly detailed, like the space cows and sheeps, I simply just love them, they are adorable! https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3245773366 [b] Sound: [/b] The soundtrack is soothing and perfectly complements the game’s relaxed vibe. The ambient sounds and gentle music create an experience that makes you feel like you’re in a cozy spaceship. The sound effects are well-done, adding to the overall atmosphere without ever being intrusive. [b] Controls: [/b] The controls are smooth with kb+m and mostly smooth with gamepad. The interface is clean and easy to navigate, making it accessible for players of all skill levels. [b] Achievements: [/b] Atm you can get up to 35 achievements and you can clear the game in 3-4+ hours. None of the achievements are missable and even without being a hardcore gamer you can get them all. [b] Overall: [/b] Cozy Space Survivors is a great blend of relaxing atmosphere and the typical auto-hitter vampire-survivors like gameplay. It has cute graphics, captivating gameplay, and a relaxing soundscape. The Dev is really a nice guy and is really committed with the community on Discord and is helping a lot with questions and things. I would recommend give it a look! When you are looking for a really relaxing rouge-lite you’re just in the right place. And in the end - a big THANK YOU to the developer who made the game available as part of the Curators Connect programm! If you like my review, you may also like my curator page! The game is very cheap, it's true. But after playing for 20 minutes it feels like I've seen it all. Yes, there are several more ships, but the things you do are all the same on the same map with the same enemies and quests, with the same flow. Additionally, there is no real variety in builds, or your decisions. You'll need a bit of everything (loot range, attack range, movement speed, attack speed, damage, regen). The only difference is which weapons you use, and it all boils down to "it's either explosions that scale from area damage, or it's lazers/bullets that scale from penetration and lazer/bullets damage", of which you'll also have a couple. So every run is also the same in terms of builds. The game rewards map knowledge, which is nice, but since there is only one map and it's small (which is ok since the run is also 10 minutes long), you'll know it after 2-3 runs. The art and sounds and humor are all very nice. If you played the demo, you saw more or less the entire game.

I found myself more interested in the developer's write-up of the game than the game itself. That's not so much a criticism of what's here, but insights into the development process and sales history aren't something you often get to see behind the curtain. *Cozy Survivors* is serviceable enough as a survivors-like game, but it doesn't bring much new to the table beyond respecting the player's time. Each run lasts around 10 minutes, and there aren't any ridiculous requirements to unlock the available content, whether that's new weapons or ships. The ships do a good job of varying the playstyle. For instance, the final ship you unlock is a robot that you direct by choosing objectives such as seeking out an upgrade or completing a quest. It definitely boosts the difficulty, as you can't be sure if it will decide to go full-on kamikaze into a fleet of enemies. It's not a strong recommendation, but I picked it up for around $0.50 in a bundle, and at that price it felt worthwhile. Either way, I'm interested in seeing what the developer comes up with next.

Cozy Space Survivors delivers exactly what it promises. A cozy, space-themed take on the Vampire Survivors formula. The progression system is well designed, and each ship has its own distinct playstyle, keeping the game feeling fresh from start to finish. The upgrades are powerful and satisfying, and I always enjoyed watching my humble little ship transform over the course of a run into a heavily weaponized machine of mass destruction. The side quests and missions are a great, giving each level a sense of purpose beyond simply surviving. They do a nice job of mixing up the gameplay and encouraging exploration. I also appreciated the charming cast of characters you meet along the way. they're cute, memorable, and add plenty of personality to the experience. For just a couple bucks, Cozy Space Survivors offers a lot of fun and is an easy recommendation from me.

I bought this in a bundle for 60 cents and now I feel like I stole from the dev! What a delightful little game 😊 Gameplay is what matters most in a game like this, and I can say that it nailed it! The main game loop has you survive the map for 10 minutes with each ship to unlock the next, for 5 ships total. Additionally, there are some quests that you can finish again with each ship. The cool thing about this is that the ships are so significantly different from each other, as opposed to just a reskin with speed/power adjustments, that after the second one you kinda relearn the game from the ground up with each one. This keeps the game fresh and challenging throughout, I was impressed at how balanced it felt, I think people who say it's repetitive stopped before trying all the ships. It would be a recommendation just for the above, but on top of it: - It really does care about your time and avoids wasting it. Continuing the point above, if it was 30 minute runs and 40 hours long, it would definitely become boring indeed. However, it is exactly as long as it needs to be, I like finishing games, but I can't finish things that are more than 15-20 hours, and even that is a struggle (poor Vampire Survivors is sitting at 20%). This took me 4-5 hours to completely finish everything at a chill pace and I feel like I could replay it at any time and still have fun. You could probably finish it in 3 hours if you rush it. - The quests in a Survivaton (I guess that's what we call them now according to Poncle, though I really REALLY hoped garlic-like would catch on 😁) are a great idea to make runs a little more purposeful. I chuckled at "Lente's boat" as soon as I saw the title as I knew what that one would be ("Spilled!" crossover). - The pixelated art is really nice and matches the vibe of the game so well, although I understand this can be subjective. I'm personally a sucker for good pixel-art. - Cute space cuteness - Chocolate! Issues I've noticed: On Steam Deck the game would crash/quit after every run, a few seconds into the game over screen. Something must be wrong with the Linux build, but you can force it to use Proton in the game's properties on Steam, which will download and run the windows version that doesn't do this. Thinky (the 5th ship) correctly goes after XP "portals" (that bring all outstanding XP to their position) when in XP hunting mode. However it completely ignores the equivalent Chocolate portals when in Choco hunting mode, making it incredibly frustrating to get them, if at all possible. This seems like a very easy fix, rebuilding the game would be more trouble than fixing this, but I'd like to see it addressed. And if it is, Thinky is also not able to specifically targer the Utah Teapot, it would make sense to add it to the quests hunting mode when it spawns.
